record.paper_title: Challenges in Truncating the Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Reduced Density Matrices Equations: Open Problems
record.original_question: How can closure approximations for time-dependent one- and two-body reduced density matrices be designed so that the propagated density matrices remain positive semidefinite and also satisfy fermionic occupation constraints, meaning natural orbital occupation numbers stay between zero and one, while avoiding unphysical negative local densities or divergent densities during electron dynamics?

evidence.quote: all RDMs are positive-semidefinite which refers to the fact that all eigenvalues of RDMs are always equal to or greater than zero.
in the case of fermionic particles, the Pauli exclusion principle enforces natural orbital occupation numbers to be less than or equal to one [23]. Thus, they have to remain between zero and one.

We conclude that, a possible way to make progress in the application of the BBGKY hierarchy is to make sure that positive-semidefiniteness of the density matrices and the fermionic constraints on the occupation numbers is built into the equations.

artifact.category_tag: Reduced density matrices and BBGKY hierarchy
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of designing two-body BBGKY closures that exactly preserve N-representability (positive semidefiniteness of RDMs and fermionic occupation bounds) during time propagation remains open. Existing time-dependent 2-RDM methods (e.g. TD2RDM with cluster-expansion or contraction-based reconstruction functionals for the 3-RDM) achieve approximate stability only by combining the closure with auxiliary dynamical purification or correction algorithms that enforce positivity and occupation bounds, rather than by an intrinsically constraint-preserving closure. Recent works (2014–2025) explicitly state that approximate enforcement of N-representability is essential for stable propagation, indicating the exact preservation problem is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: N-representability-driven reconstruction of the two-electron RDM for a real-time TD electronic structure method
status_evidence.snippet: approximately enforcing N-representability during time evolution is essential for achieving stable solutions
status_evidence.claim: Current closures only approximately enforce N-representability and require purification.

status_evidence.title: Propagating two-particle reduced density matrices without wavefunctions
status_evidence.snippet: necessary N-representability conditions are enforced during integration by means of a purification procedure
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art TD2RDM relies on purification rather than intrinsically constraint-preserving closures.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Time-Dependent Density-Matrix Approach
status_evidence.snippet: two minimally invasive and energy-conserving correction algorithms are proposed involving dynamical purification of the truncated BBGKY hierarchy solution
status_evidence.claim: Active research still proposes correction algorithms, indicating the exact problem is unresolved.
